exposure: prior surgical history in the household
concerns about increasing Cesarean section rates
specific perceived barriers (financial costs, geographic distance, lack of quality of care)
outcome: self-reported perceptions of access to surgical and anesthesia care
community trends regarding surgical care utilization
cohort: Individuals from 50 different households who presented to the Trifinio Center for Human Development (TCHD) in Southwestern Guatemala and consented to participate were interviewed.
finding: The study identified a significant demand for essential surgeries in rural Southwestern Guatemala and highlighted financial costs, geographic distance, and lack of quality of care as the primary perceived barriers to accessing surgical and anesthesia care.
mod_finding: Eighty percent of households expressed a preference for hospital birth and concerns about increasing rates of Cesarean sections, which was also reported as one of the most commonly perceived procedures.
